title: The carrier was already immune to the 2026 filename CVEs; the binder was not immune to ambiguity, and my first fix traded precision for recall and had to be reverted

web_context.CVE-2026-91140: CVSS 9.6, Progress DataDirect ARCGenAI: shell metacharacters in an OpenAPI filename reach a shell cleanup routine
web_context.CVE-2026-40088 / GHSA-2763-cj5r-c79m: PraisonAI passes workflow/LLM input to subprocess.run(shell=True)
web_context.CVE-2026-25130 (CAI find_file): a data parameter beginning with a dash reaches find's -exec; fix is to require the value not start with a dash
web_context.CVE-2026-2256 (MS-Agent): shell tool behind a denylist, bypassable by obfuscation
web_context.ATR-2026-02601: general form: a value documented as DATA that reaches a binary as an OPTION
web_context.lethal_trifecta: private data + untrusted content + external communication; prompt injection called architectural rather than patchable

finding_1_the_design_was_already_right.measurement: admitted_confinement_execution_v1 and brokered_workspace_execution_v1 contain no shell=True and no os.system; execution is subprocess.run(list)
finding_1_the_design_was_already_right.consequence: '$(whoami)' and '; rm -rf /' inside a filename are characters in a filename, not code
finding_1_the_design_was_already_right.note: this is architectural, not a guard that can be bypassed by obfuscation. It is the one area of this project that does not have the 2026 vulnerability class.

finding_2_two_silent_binder_defects.now: resolves against the filesystem, longest existing token first; binds the whole name
any dash-leading token refuses the whole binding; under argv an option is not injectable but it makes positional binding undecidable
refused when a metacharacter appears anywhere in the goal

finding_3_what_is_still_open.command_substitution_fallback: '/tmp/$(whoami).txt' still binds '/tmp/$(whoami'. Resolution finds no such file and the binder falls through to the old non-space regex. Harmless under argv execution; it means 'resolution beats shape' holds only when resolution SUCCEEDS.
finding_3_what_is_still_open.spaced_filename_end_to_end: the binder now binds it correctly, but a candidate reached by words rather than by verb still carries a goal_regex written for the teaching sentence, so recall returns None. Pinned failing.

finding_4_the_fix_that_had_to_be_reverte.change: let positional binding run for every candidate, not only verb-selected ones
finding_4_the_fix_that_had_to_be_reverte.what_it_fixed: the spaced-filename end-to-end path answered correctly
finding_4_the_fix_that_had_to_be_reverte.why: it made the system answer where it had previously refused. Widening where the binder is consulted is a recall/precision trade with the wrong default for a system whose value is that it refuses rather than guesses.
finding_4_the_fix_that_had_to_be_reverte.status: reverted in the same round. Recorded so it is not retried.

the_general_lesson: a fix that raises coverage while lowering correctness is not a fix. The spaced-file bug was real and is still open, and the honest response is to leave it open with a failing test rather than to buy it with three regressions and a worse baseline. The second attempt must be narrower: make the WORD-indexed path produce a usable regex, not make the positional path fire everywhere.
what_is_real: the executor cannot be shell-injected, by construction
spaced filenames bind whole when the binder is reached
dash-leading and pipeline-shaped sentences refuse rather than truncate
the refusal is scoped to the sentence, so ordinary arguments still work
what_is_not_real: that fixing the binder fixes recall -- the word-indexed path still loses spaced files
that a binder-level fix is reachable from the verb path for every candidate
that this project could survive being made more permissive
